subject: earth_science
name: Earth & space science
review_note: Draft written for Quark. Grade levels are typical North American placements and vary by curriculum. Needs review by a subject teacher before it is treated as authoritative.
taxonomy_note: No earth-science error-code list exists yet. Each misconception names the science taxonomy (physics, chemistry or biology) its code comes from. Needs review.

topics.name: Weather and seasons
learning_goals: Observe and record daily weather.
Describe patterns across the seasons.

misconceptions.description: Records a feeling instead of an observation.
Uses vague weather words.

example_problems.prompt: Name two things you can measure about the weather.
example_problems.answer: Temperature and rainfall (also wind speed, cloud cover)

topics.name: Sun, Moon and the day-night cycle
learning_goals: Explain day and night with Earth's rotation.
Describe the apparent motion of the Sun across the sky.
key_concepts: The Sun does not move around Earth

misconceptions.description: Explains day and night by the Sun moving around Earth.
misconceptions.example: 'Night is when the Sun goes around to the other side.'

misconceptions.description: Mixes up rotation and revolution.
misconceptions.example: 'Earth revolves on its axis every day.'

example_problems.answer: Earth rotating on its axis once about every 24 hours

topics.name: Rocks, minerals and soil
learning_goals: Describe properties of rocks, minerals and soils.
Explain how soil forms.

misconceptions.description: Identifies a mineral by colour alone.
misconceptions.example: 'It is gold because it is yellow.'

misconceptions.description: Confuses rocks and minerals.

example_problems.prompt: Which is harder on the Mohs scale, talc or quartz?

topics.name: The water cycle
learning_goals: Describe evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
Explain the Sun's role in the water cycle.

misconceptions.description: Thinks clouds are made of water vapour.
Orders the cycle wrongly.

example_problems.prompt: What process turns water vapour into cloud droplets?

topics.name: Weathering, erosion and deposition
learning_goals: Distinguish weathering, erosion and deposition.
Describe how water, wind and ice shape land.

misconceptions.description: Uses weathering and erosion as the same thing.
Thinks landforms never change.

example_problems.prompt: A river carries sand to the sea and drops it. What is the dropping called?

topics.name: Seasons and Moon phases
learning_goals: Explain the seasons using Earth's tilt.
Explain the phases of the Moon and eclipses.
key_concepts: Angle of sunlight and day length

misconceptions.description: Explains seasons by Earth's distance from the Sun.
misconceptions.example: 'Summer is when Earth is closest to the Sun.'

misconceptions.description: Explains Moon phases by Earth's shadow.
misconceptions.example: 'The crescent is Earth's shadow on the Moon.'

example_problems.prompt: Why is it summer in the Northern Hemisphere in July?
example_problems.answer: The Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, so sunlight is more direct and days are longer

topics.name: The solar system and gravity
learning_goals: Describe the Sun, planets, moons and other bodies.
Explain how gravity keeps objects in orbit.
key_concepts: Gravity depends on mass and distance

misconceptions.description: Thinks there is no gravity in space.
misconceptions.example: 'Astronauts float because there is no gravity.'

misconceptions.description: Gets the order of planets wrong.

example_problems.prompt: Why do astronauts on the space station feel weightless?
example_problems.answer: They and the station are in free fall together around Earth; gravity is still acting

topics.name: The rock cycle
learning_goals: Describe igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.
Explain the processes linking them.

misconceptions.description: Thinks rocks are created from nothing or destroyed.
Mixes up rock types and how they form.

example_problems.prompt: How does sedimentary rock become metamorphic rock?
example_problems.answer: Heat and pressure change it without melting it

topics.name: Atmosphere, weather systems and climate
learning_goals: Describe layers and composition of the atmosphere.
Distinguish weather from climate and explain air masses and fronts.

misconceptions.description: Uses weather and climate interchangeably.
Thinks the Sun heats air mainly directly rather than through the ground.
misconceptions.example: 'Air is warmest high up because it is closer to the Sun.'

example_problems.prompt: What is the difference between weather and climate?
example_problems.answer: Weather is conditions over hours or days; climate is the average pattern over many years

topics.name: Plate tectonics, earthquakes and volcanoes
learning_goals: Describe Earth's layers and tectonic plates.
Relate plate boundaries to earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the mantle is a liquid ocean of magma.
misconceptions.example: 'Plates float on a sea of lava.'

misconceptions.description: Matches the wrong landform to a boundary type.
misconceptions.example: Mid-ocean ridges form at convergent boundaries

example_problems.prompt: What kind of plate boundary forms a mid-ocean ridge?

topics.name: Fossils and geologic time
learning_goals: Use the law of superposition to order rock layers.
Explain how fossils and radiometric dating show Earth's history.

misconceptions.description: Assumes rock layers are always in age order even after folding or faulting.
misconceptions.example: Calls the top layer youngest in an overturned fold

misconceptions.description: Thinks humans and non-avian dinosaurs lived at the same time.

example_problems.prompt: In undisturbed layers, which layer is oldest?

topics.name: The greenhouse effect and climate change
learning_goals: Explain the greenhouse effect.
Use evidence to describe human impacts on climate and possible responses.

misconceptions.description: Confuses the greenhouse effect with ozone depletion.
misconceptions.example: 'Climate change is caused by the ozone hole.'

misconceptions.description: Uses one cold day as evidence against warming.
misconceptions.example: 'It snowed in April, so the climate isn't warming.'

example_problems.prompt: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth's surface?
example_problems.answer: They absorb infrared radiation given off by Earth and re-emit some back toward the surface

topics.name: Earth's resources and human impact
learning_goals: Classify resources as renewable or non-renewable.
Evaluate the environmental effects of using them.

misconceptions.description: Gives an opinion without evidence.
Classifies a resource wrongly.
misconceptions.example: 'Coal is renewable because there is a lot of it.'

example_problems.prompt: Is natural gas renewable or non-renewable? Why?
example_problems.answer: Non-renewable: it forms over millions of years

topics.name: Stars, galaxies and the universe
learning_goals: Describe the life cycle of stars.
Describe galaxies and evidence for an expanding universe.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a light-year is a unit of time.
Thinks stars burn by combustion.

example_problems.answer: The distance light travels in one year (about 9.5 x 10^12 km)
